title: Target projection model transport for ordinary finite reduction
statement: Let C and C' be small categories with Grothendieck topologies J and J'. Let L : Sh(J) → Sh(J') have right adjoint V with adjunction adj : L ⊣ V and preserve finite limits, and let F : InverseImageData L be the supplied constant-coefficient algebraic inverse-image data. For every commutative Noetherian ring A, ideal I, and n : ℕ, pull F (completedMap F A I) followed by change(projection J' A I n) is naturally isomorphic to change(projection J A I n) followed by pull F (constantMap F (A / I^(n+1))).

proof.text: The definition of completedMap as a limit lift gives completedMap F A I followed by projection J' A I n equal to F.rings.map (projection J A I n) followed by constantMap F (A / I^(n+1)), by limit.lift_π.

Apply the already proved generic finiteInverseScalar_exists helper in ConstantCompletionOrdinaryFinitePullExistence to projection J A I n. This helper uses the normalized module adjunction at both rings: the restriction square is an isomorphism on underlying sheaves, its right mate is invertible by the normalized transpose equation, and conjugacy makes the scalar-extension mate invertible. It yields an isomorphism between (F.algebra (completed J A I)).modules followed by change(F.rings.map projection) and change(projection) followed by (F.algebra (finite J A I n)).modules. The helper is imported with import all; its proof is complete, not an assumption.

Use the already proved finiteScalarComposite_exists helper twice. Each scalar-composition isomorphism is uniqueness of left adjoints applied to the composite tensor adjunction, transported through resCompIso. First identify change(completedMap) followed by change(target projection) with change of their composite, using the projection equation. Then expand that composite as change(F.rings.map source projection) followed by change(constantMap). Whisker the two scalar-composition isomorphisms by the completed algebraic module inverse image, and whisker the inverse-image/scalar comparison by change(constantMap). Their composite is the required natural isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryReducedPull_targetProjectionIso
    (V : Sheaf J' (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf J (Type u)) (adj : L ⊣ V)
    [PreservesFiniteLimits L] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((pull F (completedMap F A I) ⋙ change (projection J' A I n)) ≅
      (change (projection J A I n) ⋙
        pull F (constantMap F (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)))))

statement_change.old_statement: For the constant-completion coefficient data, the completed pullback followed by change of scalars along the target projection is naturally isomorphic to change(projection J A I n) followed by pullback along constantMap F (A / I^(n+1)).
statement_change.what: Restore the geometric inverse-image hypotheses of Stacks 03EL. InverseImageData L alone transports ring and module operations but does not assert an adjunction or colimit preservation. Counterexample: take C2-invariants from C2-sets to sets, A = ℤ, I = (2), n = 0, and the completed module ℤ₂ with sign action. Constants and finite limits are preserved and algebraic lifts exist. The completed coefficient ring has trivial action, so completedMap is the identity. The source functor gives (ℤ₂^C2)/2 = 0, while the finite model gives (ℤ₂/2)^C2 = ℤ/2. Thus the original generality is false, even with left exactness. Restore the specified right adjoint and finite-limit preservation, as already assumed by ordinaryReducedPull_transport and the reviewed source-side correction. No definition or target statement changes.
